misclassified_entities.reason: The EVM opcode dispatcher is internal to the client execution context. It dispatches opcodes within the same process/thread - this is not an external trust boundary crossing.
Contract execution context is internal to the EVM. The currently executing contract code runs within the same execution environment, not crossing a trust boundary.
A contract implementing replay protection is internal EVM code. It's not an external entity - it's the contract code being executed within the EVM.
The caller contract invoking a precompile is within the same EVM execution context. The trust boundary is at transaction submission, not at the internal call to precompile.
Client implementation teams are human entities involved in development process, not entities that send data into the running system at runtime.
Network operators run nodes but do not directly send data into the protocol. They are the operators of the system, not external data sources crossing trust boundaries.
Core developers are involved in governance and EIP selection, not runtime data flow. They don't send data into the executing system.
EIP authors propose protocol changes through governance, not runtime data. They are not external entities in the threat model sense.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User or application submitting transactions via JSON-RPC or P2P gossip. Transaction data is arbitrary and untrusted. First byte detection must correctly distinguish typed vs legacy transactions. All transaction fields must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Signer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User or wallet application signing transactions. The signer creates signatures over transaction data including type byte for typed transactions. Signatures prove control of private key but don't indicate trustworthy intent.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P network peer submitting blocks for validation in Homestead fork. Peer identity is not authenticated. All blocks must be fully validated including PoW verification before acceptance.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External account that signed and submitted transaction in Homestead. Signature provides authentication of sender address. All transaction validation checks (gas, nonce, balance, EOA) must pass before execution.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Miner
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miner producing blocks with proof-of-work in Homestead. PoW verification ensures computational work was performed. Miners could attempt to manipulate timestamps or include invalid transactions - full validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The deposit contract at 0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa is a deployed immutable contract. Its code is trusted to emit correctly formatted deposit events. However, deposit data still requires format validation before processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The beacon chain receiving and processing deposit requests. The consensus layer is a separate but coordinated system. Communication follows defined protocols (EIP-7685). Trust is based on shared protocol specification but data format must be validated at boundaries.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transaction bytes require type detection via first byte. Typed transactions [0x00-0x7f] and legacy [0xc0-0xfe] must be correctly identified and routed. Invalid types must be rejected.
Signer must include type byte in signed data for typed transactions to prevent cross-type signature reuse attacks. Signature verification must reconstruct the same signing data.
Block from peer requires full validation: header checks, ommer validation (max 2, age 1-6), transaction execution, root hash verification. PoW must be verified via Ethash.
Transaction validation in Homestead: gas availability, nonce match, balance >= gas*price + value, sender must be EOA. Invalid transactions rejected before execution.
Miner PoW must be validated via Ethash hashimoto_light(). Mix digest must match. Result must meet difficulty target. Difficulty calculation includes difficulty bomb.

Deposit contract logs require strict format validation: exactly 576 bytes, correct offsets (pubkey=160, withdrawal_creds=256, amount=320, signature=384, index=512), correct sizes. Invalid format raises InvalidBlock.

Requests hash commitment in block header ensures consistency between execution and consensus layers. SHA256 hash chain provides integrity verification. Request type bytes (0x00, 0x01, 0x02) must be correct.
